title: InstructionManifest

channel.description: The instruction channel of the account's adapter: none is handed no text.

layer.description: A layer of a run's standing instructions, in the order the text holds them: user (the orientation block, then owned instructions), team-bank, project, session, persona (a bot's), always-on (always-on skills).

characters.description: The characters the layer holds in the text: its parts, with the two line breaks between each two of them.

id.description: What the part is, within its layer: orientation for the orientation block, else the id of the thing it renders.

version.description: The version of what the part renders, where it has one (a catalogue entry's); null where it has none.

items.description: A part of a layer as the manifest names it: its id, its version, and its length in characters.

parts.description: The layer's parts, in the order the text holds them.

items.description: A layer of the composed text: which, the characters it holds there, and its parts.

layers.description: The layers the text holds, in their fixed order; a layer that gave nothing, or whose parts were all left out, is not listed.

name.description: A skill's name, by the Agent Skills rule: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -, with no leading, trailing or doubled hyphen. Refused as invalid_params, the issue's params naming the rule skill-name and its reason.

repository.description: The identity of the repository the member was read from: its source's, or the trusted repository's.

path.description: The member's folder in that repository, from its root; . when the root is itself the skill.

oneOf.description: The repository the member was read from, by its identity, and the member's folder there.

repository.description: The identity of the repository the manifest says the member was copied from.

path.description: The member's folder in that repository, as the manifest names it.

anyOf.description: The commit the member was copied at, as the manifest names it: its object name, full or abbreviated.

licence.description: The licence the manifest names, an SPDX identifier where it gives one; null when it names none.

oneOf.description: What a provenance manifest beside the member names: the repository and folder it was copied from, the commit and the licence.

anyOf.description: Where a member comes from, which the readiness overlay is keyed by (repository identity and folder path): the repository it was read from, or what a provenance manifest beside a copy names.

origin.description: Where the skill comes from, as its member's origin: null for one of the own directory with no provenance manifest, or of a repository with no identity.

anyOf.description: A git commit's full object name: 40 lowercase hexadecimal digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository.

commit.description: The commit of the source snapshot it was read from; null for a member linked live (the own directory, a trusted repository).

items.description: An always-on skill the composition appended: its name, its origin and the commit it was read at.

alwaysOn.description: The always-on skills the text holds, in the order it holds them.

anyOf.description: A skill set's fingerprint: it covers the members' names, folders, origins and snapshot commits, whether each is native and always-on, and the hidden native names, so two sets with one fingerprint hold the same; a provider process spawned under another is not reused.

skillSetFingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the run's skill set; null while none is resolved for it.

unreadRegistries.description: The registries the orientation block could not read in time, each rendered as could not be read; empty when every one was read.

layer.description: A layer of a run's standing instructions, in the order the text holds them: user (the orientation block, then owned instructions), team-bank, project, session, persona (a bot's), always-on (always-on skills).

id.description: What the part is, within its layer: orientation for the orientation block, else the id of the thing it renders.

reason.description: Why a composed part is not in the text: channel-none (the account's adapter has no instruction channel, so it is handed no text), or over-cap (the text was over the channel's character cap, and owned instructions are left out last first until it fits).

items.description: A part the layers gave that the text does not hold, and why.

leftOut.description: The parts the layers gave that the text does not hold, each with why.

description: What a composition of standing instructions holds: the channel, per layer its parts' ids, versions and characters, the always-on skills with origins and commits, the skill set's fingerprint, the registries the orientation block could not read, and what was left out and why.
